articles.summary: CI/CD for GTM means every change to enrichment, scoring, routing and sequences ships as a pull request that is planned, checked, approved, deployed on merge, logged and reversible. What each software CI/CD step becomes for go-to-market, and how to set it up on Cargo.
articles.title: CI/CD for GTM: Continuous Deployment for Go-to-Market

articles.summary: How Cargo holds a go-to-market pull request that would send or spend more than set limits until a reviewer adds the cargo:approve-impact label: the thresholds, what counts as high impact, who should approve, and what the gate does not catch.
articles.title: Require Approval Before a High-Impact Go-to-Market Change Goes Live

articles.summary: How to test a change to enrichment, scoring, routing or outreach before it runs on every lead: check the project offline, dry run an action, read the plan on the pull request, ship the play switched off and pilot it on 50 records, evaluate agents, and use a second workspace as staging.
articles.title: Test a Go-to-Market Change Before It Reaches Production
